description: HTTP/2: cancelling one `respondWithFile()` download crashes the server (NULL dereference in `StreamPipe`)
overview: A NULL pointer dereference in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client crash the server, over both TLS and cleartext, by cancelling file downloads. When the server serves a file with `stream.respondWithFile()` or `stream.respondWithFD()` and the client cancels the request, a `StreamPipe` used for the transfer is torn down in an order that leaves a NULL pointer which is then dereferenced, aborting the process. No crafted frames are needed, and a handful of cancelled requests against a default file-serving handler is enough. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
